analysis:
MARKET REGIME: SPY is in confirmed uptrend (+0.6% vs SMA50, 20d slope +2.01%), which is supportive of the existing long book. No reason to reduce defensively on macro grounds alone.

EXISTING POSITION REVIEW:
• LII (-7.94%): This is the most urgent concern. Entry at $575.57, current $529.88. LII's typical ATR runs ~3-4% of price (~$17-23/share). A 1.5x ATR stop set at entry would land near $540-555. At $529.88, the stock is likely BELOW its original stop level. HVAC sector faces margin headwinds from input costs and slower residential demand. Thesis appears to be breaking. Strongly recommend exiting LII at market open to enforce stop discipline — sitting on an 8% loss in a concentrated position while hoping for recovery is exactly the behavior this strategy is designed to avoid. This would free ~$10,600 and reduce the book to 5 positions.
• FDS (-4.91%): Uncomfortable but within stop range. FDS screens well (fwd P/E 12.53, PEG 1.15, 26% of 52w range, basing). The current position is sub-optimal sizing; hold unless the stop is hit.
• CI (-1.93%): Minor drawdown, thesis intact. Managed care continues to face sector noise but quality metrics remain solid.
• WDAY (-1.41%): Within noise. Still basing at 21% of 52w range, screens as top candidate fundamentally.
• A and AMP: Both in slight gain, no action needed.

NEW TRADES: ZERO recommended this cycle. Capacity is the binding constraint — with only $13,426 remaining headroom and already 6 positions (above the 3-5 strategy target), a properly sized new position cannot be added without violating either the concentration cap or the 1-2% portfolio heat rule. Forcing a small, undersized position in a quality name like VEEV (best setup: PEG 0.88, D/E 1.41, basing at 24% of range) would manufacture activity, not alpha. The right move is to (1) exit LII to restore discipline and free capital, then (2) evaluate VEEV or ZBH with proper sizing once the book is at 5 positions and ~$24k headroom. Cash is a position. Patience here IS the edge.
